memory_candidates.content: When a mechanical mass-edit script needs to rewrite specific scalar values inside many JSON files without disturbing unrelated formatting, check first whether the target file is already in jq's canonical pretty-print form via `diff <(jq '.' file) file`. If identical, a jq round-trip append/edit is safe. If not (e.g. the file uses compact single-line arrays), a full jq round-trip will silently reformat EVERY array in the file to jq's default one-element-per-line style, producing a diff many times larger than the intended change and violating any 'only X changed' review requirement. Use surgical line-oriented text substitution (e.g. awk tracking a stable anchor field like a unique 'path' key) instead for files with non-canonical formatting.

A doc-lint/orphan-detection helper that enumerates 'deployed files' via `git ls-files` (tracked-files-only) is silently vacuous against a deploy target that is entirely gitignored (e.g. a repo where `/.claude/` is blanket-excluded in .gitignore with no tracked exceptions) -- the enumeration always returns zero results, so the check can never fail regardless of real violations, and this is easy to miss because the gate still reports PASS. Verify empirically before trusting such a helper: place a scratch file at the target path and confirm it appears in the enumeration's output, not just in `git status --ignored`. When the deploy target is untracked, enumerate the filesystem directly (find/ls) instead of git.

Pattern for letting a source-store script validate a deployed artifact from its own source-store location (pre-redeploy, without needing to invoke the deployed copy): `[[ -n "${REPO_ROOT:-}" ]] || . "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/deploy-root-guard.sh" || exit 1` followed by `REPO_ROOT="${REPO_ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"`. The deploy-root-guard fires only when REPO_ROOT is unset, so `REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/<script>.sh` deliberately bypasses the guard and points the script at the real repo root, letting it read/write the deployed `.claude/` tree from the source-store invocation path. Already established in check-extension-docs.sh; worth applying to any other core script that needs the same capability.
